_why: Owner ruling 2026-08-30: single-line trailing comments must be supported. app_parser's terminator test reads the RAW line, so `SELECT ...;  -- note` does not end with ';' and the statement never closes — it silently absorbs whatever follows. #1909 fixed the neighbouring case (a WHOLLY-comment line must not terminate) and did not address a comment after real SQL on the same line.

anchors._note: TRAP 3 — with a trailing comment this strips nothing, so ';' + comment ride into `sql` and reach extract_dependencies_text_fallback
the #1909 guard that must not regress
TRAP 3 consumer — splits on whitespace, treats the word after FROM/JOIN as a dependency
gate's NAIVE, non-quote-aware stripper — shared by 5 call sites, so fixing it fixes all of them
the gate mirror of the engine's terminator rule

blast_radius._note: Measured across src/ tests/ examples/ AGAINST MERGED MASTER 274a3a7cb. An earlier count of 1 was taken against a stale checkout, before #1929 merged, and was wrong by 6 — the dispatch gate caught it. Split: 1 ref in src/velostream/sql/app_parser.rs (the engine defect) and 6 in tests/unit/sql/validation/doc_sql_examples_test.rs (the gate mirror, which #1929 added). Related surfaces: strip_inline_comment 2 files / 16 refs, parse_statements 4 files / 25 refs. The ENGINE change is one site; the bulk of the work is the gate mirror plus tests.

grammar_reference._note: A SQL line comment is `--` to end of line. The ONLY exception is `--` inside a string literal, which is not a comment. app_parser has NO quote-state tracking today (grep in_string|in_quote|quote_char -> nothing); that is harmless only because the terminator asks whether a line ENDS with ';', never whether it CONTAINS one, so `WHERE sep = 'a;b';` works. Comment stripping TRUNCATES the line and destroys that property — see tests.fail_to_pass quote_aware case.

tests._note: Each must be a mutation-kill: break the code, confirm the test fails, restore, confirm it passes, log the proof in agent.log. `trailing_comment_scan_is_quote_aware` covers `SELECT * FROM t WHERE note = 'a -- b';` — a line that works TODAY and that the naive fix would break, so it is a regression guard, not a new-feature test.
